topic.title: Boosting, Weak Learning, and Classification Guarantees
topic.overview: Boosting combines imperfect predictors into a stronger classifier, but its success depends on the weak learner, loss, noise model, and number of classes. This cluster studies margins, agnostic learning, cost-sensitive formulations, and statistical guarantees. Related reliability work examines how confidence rankings affect a classifier’s ability to abstain appropriately.
topic.whyItMatters: Repeatedly improving a training objective does not guarantee robustness to noisy labels or efficient multiclass learning. Resource requirements can shift from the booster to its underlying learner, and confidence rescaling alone may not fix an incorrect ranking of predictions.
topic.evolution: Early representatives explore noisy classification and ensemble training. The 2000s work sharpens convergence and margin analyses while identifying limitations of convex boosting under noise. Recent studies quantify multiclass weak-learning costs, improve agnostic sample efficiency, and decompose errors in selective classification and boosted regression inference.
openQuestions: How can boosting tolerate realistic label noise without demanding an unrealistically strong weak learner?
Which scores correctly rank prediction reliability under distribution shift?
